title: A finite Galois extension has finitely many automorphisms and fixed field the base
statement: Let $M/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] with $\dim_kM<\infty$ which is Galois: separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and normal (for every $\beta\in M$ the minimal polynomial of $\beta$ over $k$ is a product of polynomials of degree one in $M[T]$). Let $G=\operatorname{Aut}(M/k)$ be the group of $k$-algebra automorphisms of $M$. Then $G$ is finite, of order $|G|=\dim_kM$, and its fixed field is $k$: an element $y\in M$ satisfies $\tau(y)=y$ for all $\tau\in G$ if and only if $y$ lies in (the image of) $k$.

source.place: Fields, Lemma 09I1 (fields-lemma-finite-Galois, line 2664: $|\mathrm{Aut}(E/F)|=[E:F]$ for finite Galois $E/F$) and Theorem 09DW (fields-theorem-galois-theory, line 2784: $K=L^G$ for a finite Galois extension $L/K$ with group $G$)
